narr: A slow-moving low pressure system brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms over multiple days through much of the region. Activity on the 25th was mostly concentrated across higher terrain areas of eastern AZ, fueled by MLCAPE values approaching 2000 J/kg. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours, producing rainfall accumulations of over 2 inches in less than one hour across the Miami area leading to significant flash flooding. Multiple streets became rushing currents of water, floodwaters escaped Bloody Tanks Wash in several locations and flooded businesses, there was a lot of muddy and rocky debris, and there were several minor landslides. Severe hail was observed with the thunderstorm activity as well. ||The most impactful day of this multi-day episode occurred on the 26th when widespread thunderstorm activity developed across much of south-central AZ as strong upper-level divergence from the low pressure system moved overhead. Fueled by MLCAPE values near 2000 J/kg and near 30 kts of 0-6 km shear, scattered thunderstorms developed in the Phoenix area during the mid-morning hours with increasing coverage through the afternoon hours. Initially, most of the storm reports received were large hail, however, as activity became more widespread the hazard quickly turned to flash flooding with numerous reports of water rescues. A fatality due to drowning was reported in Indian Bend Wash in Scottsdale when the individual's vehicle became submerged by significant floodwaters. A few hours after the rainfall dissipated in the Phoenix area, a new area of strong to severe thunderstorms, with very heavy rainfall, moved eastward into southern Gila County, affecting the Globe/Miami area for a second time in just over 24 hours. Gauge reports and doppler radar estimates out of the Globe area measured approximately 2��� of rain, with most of the rain occurring in less than 30 minutes. A stream gauge along Pinal Creek, just south of downtown Globe, reported a 6 foot water rise in 30 minutes. Subsequently, videos and images emerged from downtown Globe depicting catastrophic flooding as the flood wave in Pinal Creek overtopped bridges, inundated businesses, and flooded or swept away numerous vehicles. Around 800 propane tanks were also swept into the floodwaters from a nearby distribution center. Around 66 vehicles were recovered and approximately 288 tons of trash and debris, as well as 8000 cubic yards of dirt, were cleared. The flooding claimed three lives. ||Additional shower and thunderstorm activity materialized on the 27th as the low pressure system was still over southern CA. The more widespread activity was concentrated across portions of southwest AZ during the morning and early afternoon hours with instances of flash flooding reported. Additional activity did develop across south-central AZ as well, including across portions of the Phoenix area, during the afternoon hours. Coverage was more isolated compared to the 26th, but the storms still produced additional flash flooding and severe winds gusts. A thunderstorm cell once again moved through the already flood ravaged area of Globe/Miami in the afternoon. Despite rainfall amounts remaining under an inch with this storm, due to quick storm motion, flash flooding occurred once again in the area, exacerbated by the very saturated soils from the rainfall the previous two days.||Following this three-day episode, local, state, and federal disaster declarations were made for the Globe area, a disaster assistance center was opened, and approximately 600 initial and preliminary damage assessments were conducted by AZ Department of Emergency and Military Affairs, finding around 200 private and public properties were destroyed, with the rest experiencing some scale of damage. Not all events are captured in detail in this episode due to the large scale and number of the impacts. Damage cost estimates were in the millions.
ev: Floodwater from heavy rain northeast of Globe traveled downstream within Ramboz Wash to Gilson Wash and then all the way to San Carlos. At some point within these washes a swift water rescue was made by San Carlos Apache Police and Fire Departments. Video showed a single individual hanging in a tree above their totaled SUV in the floodwaters. A separate post showed flooding across Route 6 near mile post 7, stemming from the floodwaters in Gilson Wash, leading to the closure of the road. Not far from this location, a streamflow gauge measured an 8.3 ft peak stage height at 2240MST after initially rising beginning around 2125MST.
Social media video shows Fortuna Wash in Fortuna Foothills with quick flowing water. No damages or injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gauge along Indian Bend Wash at Shea Boulevard recorded a water level above the alarm stage level of 2 feet, with the stage peaking at 3.02 feet and likely flooding the downstream greenbelt area of the wash and low water crossings. Timing estimated based on the period when water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage level. No damages or injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge along Jackrabbit Wash recorded a water level above the alarm stage level of 2.9 feet, with a peak stage of 3.78 feet. Exceeding alarm stage corresponds to likely flooding of Wickenburg Road located approximately 5.1 miles downstream of the gauge. There was an extended period of greater than 900 cfs with flow peaking at 1560 cfs, resulting in likely greater than 1.5 feet of flowing water over the road. Timing estimated based on the period when water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage level as well as travel time for the water to reach Wickenburg Road. No damages or injuries reported.
Water rescue along North 40th Street due to flooding in Cudia City Wash. No injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge along Sonoran Wash recorded a water level above the alarm stage of 2.0 feet, and peaked at a stage of 3.57 feet. Based on the peak stage level, the unbridged crossing at North Valley Parkway was likely flooded based on studies and mapping by the flood control district. Timing estimated based on the period when water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage level as well as travel time for the water to reach North Valley Parkway. No damages or injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge along Cave Creek Wash measured a water level above the alarm stage level of 3 feet, and reached a peak stage of 3.65 feet. Based on the peak stage 7th Avenue was likely impassable, based on studies and mapping by the flood control district. Timing estimated based on the period when water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage level. No damages or injuries reported.

Video showed 7th Avenue along Cave Creek Wash was impassable due to flooding. A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge located near the roadway measured water levels above the alarm stage level of 3 feet, with a peak level of 5.07 feet. Timing estimated based on the period when water level exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage. No damages or injuries reported.
Video showed Loomis Ave in Miami was a raging river with a foot of water rapidly moving down the street. No damages or injuries reported.

Video showed significant flash flooding along US-60 near Grover Canyon Rd with a few feet of water in front of the Miami Regional Training Center with water up to the hoods of several cars. No injuries reported.
US-60 closed between Mile-marker 243 and Mile-marker 247, from Miami to AZ 188, due to flooding. A photo also showed a flooded Miami Ave in downtown Miami. No damages or injuries reported.
Video from Miami Memorial Library showed several inches of water rapidly moving down Adonis Avenue. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Video showed water raging down Chisholm Avenue in Miami. A couple of large black cylinder items were swept down the road by the floodwaters. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
John Cabot Road in Sun City was flooded. No damages or injuries reported.
Water rescue reported near the area of 99th Avenue and Thunderbird Road in Sun City. No injuries reported.
Water rescue reported near the area of Olive Avenue and 103rd Avenue in Peoria. No injuries reported.
Water rescue reported in the area of 7th Avenue and Elwood Street in Phoenix. No injuries reported.
Water rescue reported in the vicinity of South 20th Street and University Drive in Phoenix. No injuries reported.
Water rescue reported in the vicinity of North 13th Street and East Hatcher Road in Phoenix. No injuries reported.
Water rescue reported in the vicinity of North 227th Avenue and West Patton Road in Wittmann. No injuries reported.
Camera shot showed stranded cars on the eastbound ramp onto I-10 near Buckeye Road in Phoenix. No injuries reported.
Water rescue reported in the vicinity of South 32nd street and East Air Lane on the outskirts of Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport. No injuries reported.
Video showed significant flooding on Richwood Avenue from the Hesperus Wash in Fountain Hills. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Flooding along Fort McDowell Road from Colony Wash. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
State Route 238 closed westbound near S 99th Ave in Mobile due to flooding. No damages or injuries reported.

Video showed major flooding at North Gary Road about 1/4 mile north San Tan Foothills High School in Queen Creek with approximately 2 feet of rushing water and cars stranded. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
Waymo taxi car stuck in the floodwaters near the area of 32nd and Washington Street in Phoenix. No injuries reported.
Video showed about 6-12 inches of water flowing along Main Street in Florence. No damages or injuries reported.
Video showed considerable flow along Hunt Highway in Florence with a vehicle stuck in the floodwaters. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
Reports of Aberdeen Rd. being impassable. No damages or injuries reported.
Fast flowing water along Vanwinkle Avenue in Miami. No damages or injuries reported.
Fast flowing water through Six Shooter Canyon wash, inundating low water crossings including Beer Tree Crossing. No damages or injuries reported.
US 60 impassable near the Miami area. No damages or injuries reported.

A damage assessment showed evidence of floodwaters escaping Bloody Tanks Wash near the US-60 bridge. Photos showed Reppy Ave just south of US-60 had significant flooding with the road covered curb to burb in a few inches of mud and rocks. No damages or injuries reported.
Water rescue reported by Phoenix Fire Dispatch Center. No damages or injuries reported.

A Flood Control District of Maricopa County streamflow gauge on Skunk Tank Wash at 7th Ave recorded a water level above the designated alarm stage of 4.2 ft and reached a peak stage height of 5.48 ft at 1940MST. With water levels above alarm stage, multiple low water crossings became impassable. Timing based on when water level rose above and fell below alarm stage. No damages or injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge along Waterman Wash at Rainbow Valley Road in Buckeye had water levels rise above the alarm stage level of 3.1 feet, with the stage peaking at 5.54 feet, and made low-water crossings downstream of the gauge impassable, including Tuthill and Narramore Roads. Timing was estimated based on the period water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage and time it took to reach the aforementioned road crossings. No damages or injuries reported.

Floodwaters escaped the banks of Bloody Tanks Wash and came down the streets from the north leading to significant flash flooding in downtown Miami, with lots of mud and rocky debris. Floodwaters entered businesses on Sullivan St. The floodwaters led to the collapse of the front entrance wall of the Wild Horses Saloon on Sullivan St. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

Walmart closed due to flooding with around 60% of the store flooded with a couple inches of water. Some trash pallets from behind the store also clogged the culvert under US-60, which compounded the flooding. The extent of damages to the store is unknown. No injuries reported.
An I-10 interchange with I-17 southbound was impassable due to flooding. No damages or injuries reported.

Multiple Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauges along Indian Bend Wash through Scottsdale rose above action stages and flood stages, with all low-water crossings impassable. The streamflow gauge at Indian School Rd reached 3000 cfs. Multiple water rescues were performed with broadcast videos showing multiple vehicles submerged in the floodwaters. A 38-year-old male drowned after his vehicle was completely submerged and pinned against a railing after trying to drive across the Roosevelt Street low water crossing.

Catastrophic and deadly flash flooding occurred in the Globe area following strong to severe thunderstorms that produced very high rainfall rates. Observed gauge reports and doppler radar rainfall estimates measured approximately 2 inches of rain within 30 minutes in the Globe area. A stream gauge along the typically dry Pinal Creek, just south of Downtown Globe, recorded a dramatic 6-foot rise in water in 30 minutes between 1825MST and 1855MST. This flood wave quickly moved through downtown Globe, overtopping bridges, inundating businesses, and sweeping away dozens of vehicles. Many sloped streets also became raging currents. Additionally, around 800 propane tanks were swept into the floodwaters from a distribution center along the creek. Several dozen homes and businesses were inundated with water, with some experiencing water levels of two to three feet deep. Floodwaters traveled over 15 miles north of Globe, within Pinal Creek, all the way to the Salt River and Roosevelt Lake with additional flooding impacts experienced in the Wheatfields area. A USGS gauge on Pinal Creek just south of the Salt River recorded an 8 ft water level rise and came within half a foot of reaching the gauge's historical peak. In the aftermath of the flooding, approximately 288 tons of trash and debris as well as 800 cubic yards of dirt were cleared. There were also over 60 vehicles damaged or destroyed, with some of them wedged under bridges. The flooding resulted in three fatalities, all from vehicles swept away. In response to the catastrophic flash flooding, Globe's Mayor, Al Gameros, declared a State of Emergency for Globe on the afternoon of the 27th followed shortly by an Arizona State of Emergency declaration from Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs. Preliminary damage assessments performed in the subsequent days had estimated damage costs of approximately $25 million.
